title: A 1,000-Year-Old Tower With an 80-Tonne Top
description: The Brihadeeswarar temple in Thanjavur, built by the Chola emperor Rajaraja I.

scenes.narration: More than a thousand years ago, a king built a temple tower that still stands sixty-six metres tall.
scenes.image_prompt: towering granite temple vimana of Brihadeeswarar temple against a blue sky

scenes.narration: It's 1010 CE in Thanjavur. The Chola emperor Rajaraja the First has just completed the Brihadeeswarar temple.
scenes.image_prompt: Chola emperor in royal attire before a giant granite temple, priests and crowds, 11th century

scenes.narration: It's built mostly of granite, though there's no granite quarry close by.
scenes.image_prompt: ox carts hauling huge granite blocks across a dry South Indian landscape

scenes.narration: At the very top sits a huge capstone, said to weigh around eighty tonnes.
scenes.image_prompt: giant stone dome capstone on top of a pyramidal temple tower, workers small beside it

scenes.narration: How did they lift it? One popular theory: a very long earthen ramp.
scenes.image_prompt: long earthen ramp leading up to an unfinished temple tower, elephants and workers pulling a huge stone

scenes.narration: Inside, the walls carry Chola paintings and inscriptions.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Chola fresco paintings on temple walls inside a dim corridor, oil lamps

scenes.narration: A giant Nandi bull, carved from a single stone, faces the shrine.
scenes.image_prompt: huge monolithic stone Nandi bull under a pillared pavilion in a temple courtyard

scenes.narration: It has stood for a thousand years. Which Indian temple should we explore next?
scenes.image_prompt: Brihadeeswarar temple at sunset with pilgrims in the courtyard
